title: Rabbi Elazar ben Antigenos
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: (A Palestinian Amora of the second generation.) He was the student of Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Yannai and Hyman says he always spoke in his name, as in Gittin 31a: “Which twenty-four-hour period? Rabbi Yochanan said: the twenty-four-hour period of examination; Rabbi Elazar ben Antigenos says in the name of Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Yannai: the twenty-four-hour period of setting aside.” In Chullin 9a he speaks in the name of Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Yannai; likewise Chullin 55b, where Rabbah bar bar Chana disagrees with Rabbi Elazar ben Antigenos, who spoke in the name of Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Yannai; and there, at 56b, he speaks in the name of Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Yannai: “Both this and that require examination.” In Beitzah 34a the statement reads the reverse, that Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Yannai speaks in his name; Hyman proposes the reading in Chullin, and so it is in Dikdukei Soferim. Hyman considers the same error present in Rashi and interprets Rashi as intending to correct it, so that one would not err in saying that he is a Tanna; therefore he says “so we read: Rabbi Elazar said,” etc., and with this Seder HaDorot’s difficulty is removed. In Shabbat 103b he spoke in the name of Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov; Hyman proposes Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Yannai, and so it is in the Rif and Dikdukei Soferim. Likewise we find many times in the Jerusalem Talmud that he spoke in the name of Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Yannai, as in Berakhot, chapter 2, beginning of halakhah 6; Maaserot 4:3; Gittin 3:8; and Bava Metzia 7:4. In Berakhot, chapter 5, end of halakhah 2, “Rabbi Ze’ira, Rabbi Elazar ben Antigenos in the name of Rabbi Yannai”; Hyman proposes Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Yannai.

notes.text: מע״ל is מעת לעת, a twenty-four-hour period, not an unexplained maal. Saved Davidson Gittin31a fully writes Elazar ben Antigenos and Elazar son of Yannai, supporting these connected expansions. The inspection/setting-aside alternatives remain without an invented forward/backward direction. All teacher reversals, Rashi interpretations and Eliezer ben Yaakov substitutions remain Hyman’s conjectures; בקד״ס is read as בדק״ס.

Gittin 31a ends after the named transmission;31b begins with the twenty-four-hour period of setting aside. The consulted Beitzah 34a and its Rashi both transmit Elazar son of Yannai in the name of Elazar ben Antigenos. Hyman’s reversal proposal and interpretation of Rashi remain his, alongside that directly consulted reading. Exact Rif and Dikdukei Soferim claims remain attributed.
